name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,491

clue.text: Drunk with hat getting very quietly half cut

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes one of its two halves, so one of the pair of letters is dropped

blocks.note: a top hat is a topper
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A tipsy man in a hat is getting quietly sozzled, half cut being slang for drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPPER already holds the PP; halving PP means one P goes, leaving TOPER. 'Half cut' poses as slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, so the noun sense of drunk, a person who is intoxicated, fits.

clue.text: Downtime Alison arranged in flat

indicators.note: arranging things sets them in a new order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Alison's time off has been organised into a flat, perhaps a city apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has only length and breadth and no depth is flat, as a picture or a shallow character is.

clue.text: Medley in grass serve Rafael inspired originally

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: slang for cannabis
to pour drinks is to serve them
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of tennis memories: Rafael Nadal serving on grass, inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and serve suggest tennis and Nadal, but grass is cannabis slang and serve means pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri literally means a mixture of dried petals, and figuratively any miscellaneous medley or assortment.

clue.text: Musician with yen to make garden feature

blocks.note: a rock musician
Y is the symbol for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A musician with a yearning sets about creating something for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Yen looks like a longing but is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is an arrangement of stones planted with alpines, a familiar ornamental part of a garden.

clue.text: American spies suppress account by field officer finding food

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep something held down under cover, so one piece is shut inside the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for field officer
the Central Intelligence Agency
common abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: US intelligence covers up a field officer's account in some espionage story ending in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The spies hold the account inside them, and the field officer sits by them at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Focaccia is a flat Italian bread, often topped with olive oil and herbs, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Report of small glass bottle in papers

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a phial is a small medicine bottle

explanation.surface: A news report about a little bottle turning up among some documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a folder of documents or papers kept together, so it collectively stands for papers.

clue.text: Remember what a baby sitter does

blocks.note: first meaning: to recollect or bring back to memory
second meaning, read literally: someone is summoned so they can look after the child

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the phrase: a sitter is called in order to mind the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something back into one's thoughts is to recollect it, the same as remember.

clue.text: Head is an attractive woman

blocks.note: first meaning: old British slang for the head
second meaning: dated British slang for sexually attractive women

explanation.surface: Someone's chief is a looker.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is also a British griddle cake, eaten toasted; both slang senses here are dated British.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang uses the word for the skull or head, and also for women considered sexually desirable.

clue.text: Trojan arrested in Brasilia Cathedral

indicators.note: someone arrested in a place is held there, so the letters are held inside these words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the city name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A man from Troy is detained in a cathedral in Brazil's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Trojan looks like a noun, a person, but here it is the adjective: Ilium was the Latin name for Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac can mean relating to Ilium, ancient Troy, so it is an adjective equivalent to Trojan.

clue.text: Hounds your tormentors after lesson

indicators.note: after places the words before it later in the answer, behind the school subject

blocks.note: English is a school subject or lesson
crossword setters, who torment solvers

explanation.surface: Bullies pursue someone once school is out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hounds looks like a verb, as tormentors would, but it is the plural noun; the setters themselves are the tormentors.
explanation.definitionFit: English setters are a breed of gun dog, and hound is used loosely for any hunting dog.

clue.text: What a landlady uses by implication involves one litre in a deception

indicators.note: a thing that involves another takes it in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: an optic is the measuring device fixed to an upturned spirit bottle behind a British bar
an allusion is an indirect, implied reference
I for one, L for litre

explanation.surface: A pub landlady relies on hints and implications to pull off some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic, in a British pub, dispenses a fixed measure of spirits; the one litre goes in after the first two letters of the implication word.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a visual trick that misleads the eye, hence a deception of the senses.

clue.text: Old boy supplants artist in heart of country girl

indicators.note: to supplant is to take another's place, so one piece is swapped out for another
the heart of a word is its middle, telling where the replaced letters sit

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil
Royal Academician
a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: A former pupil displaces a painter at the centre of some national affair, in the girl's affections perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy means a former pupil of a school, and RA marks a Royal Academician; the country is in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobel is a female first name, so it names a girl; crosswords often define names this way.

clue.text: Unusual play with Act 1 rewritten

indicators.note: a rewritten text has its material set down afresh, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the numeral 1 reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: A drama whose opening act has been redrafted would be out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not representative of the type, a direct synonym of unusual or uncharacteristic.

clue.text: Heard cleric cry loudly in quick service

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by ear, so the words are spelt by how they are pronounced

blocks.note: a canon is a cathedral clergyman
to bawl is to shout or wail

explanation.surface: A clergyman is overheard wailing during a hurried church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Service means a tennis serve, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a very fast, powerful first serve is called a cannonball, so it is a quick service.

clue.text: Parliamentary procedures that maybe passed before breakfast!

definitions.text: Parliamentary procedures that maybe passed before breakfast!

blocks.note: straight sense: formal proposals tabled by MPs in the House of Commons
joke sense: bowel movements, also called motions, that occur first thing in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: These are motions tabled in the Commons that are rarely debated; the exclamation flags the lavatory pun on motions being passed early.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK Parliament, MPs table such motions to register opinions, which matches parliamentary procedures, while the clue jokes about morning bowel habits.

clue.text: Unaware of patent involving light metal

indicators.note: a thing involving another wraps it up, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: patent as an adjective means plain to see
the chemical symbol for lithium, the lightest metal

explanation.surface: Someone does not know about a patent application that involves a lightweight metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Patent looks like the noun for an invention licence but is the adjective meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means having no awareness of what is going on around one, so it equals unaware.

clue.text: Plants that can make you smart?

definitions.text: Plants that can make you smart?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that makes a person clever or well-dressed
setter's reading: a weed whose hairs cause the skin to smart, that is to hurt

explanation.walkthrough: Smart here is the verb for a sharp burning pain, not cleverness or elegance; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: These common weeds have tiny hairs that inject irritants, making brushed skin burn and itch painfully.

clue.text: Doctor's operation after face-lift for Candy?

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises letters, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: mug is slang for face
standard abbreviation for doctor
short form of operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon carries out cosmetic surgery for a patient named Candy.
explanation.walkthrough: The face-lift is not surgery but the face word turned upside down in this down entry, placed before the doctor's operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy sweet, and candy is the American word for sweets.

clue.text: Spooner’s call for additional wine creates distress

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: a request for extra tent, a dark red Spanish wine; with its first sounds swapped

explanation.surface: Asking for another glass leads to upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is a deep red wine from Spain, once used as communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment and distress both mean severe mental or physical suffering, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Salve for state burial the Queen discarded

indicators.note: what is discarded is thrown away, so these letters are taken out

blocks.note: O is an old abbreviation for Ohio, a US state
interment is the act of burying the dead
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Pomp for a state funeral is dropped once the monarch is no longer involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State burial' reads as one phrase, but state is a separate piece; ER is the usual shorthand for the Queen, removed from the burial word.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing medicinal cream applied to skin, the same thing as an ointment.

clue.text: Chemical on egg - quite the reverse

blocks.note: a nit is a louse egg
re means about or on, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A chemical sits on an egg, or rather the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'A on B' puts A above B; 'quite the reverse' swaps which piece goes on top, rather than turning letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, saltpetre, a chemical compound used in gunpowder and as a fertiliser.

clue.text: Dick has to check over rector’s hedge

indicators.note: something that has another thing holds it within itself

blocks.note: a private dick is a private investigator
R is the abbreviation for rector
to vet is to examine carefully

explanation.surface: A detective must inspect the vicar's garden boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick is slang for a detective. The investigator holds the rector, and the checking verb follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is a dense evergreen shrub very commonly grown as a garden hedge in Britain.

clue.text: Troubles racialist oddly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd positions means only the even-numbered letters are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Racial tension is causing trouble but is strangely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail someone is to trouble or afflict them, so the third-person verb matches troubles.

clue.text: Son comes in to reform illegal veto in electoral system

indicators.note: what is illegal is not in proper order, so these letters break their lawful arrangement

blocks.note: to reform something is to alter it
a son of a place is a native of it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son joins a campaign to overturn an unlawful veto on changing the voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: Son is not S here: it means a native, as in a son of the soil, and it comes in to join the reform word. The 2011 UK referendum rejected this system.
explanation.definitionFit: The alternative vote is a preferential voting method where voters rank candidates, so it is a type of electoral system.

clue.text: Good-natured pollster embraces birds

indicators.note: a phrase that embraces something holds it within its arms, so the letters lie inside these words

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A kindly opinion surveyor gives some birds a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Redpolls are small finches with a red crown patch, so they are a kind of bird.

clue.text: Examines balls after dropping second base

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: testicles, colloquially balls
e is the base of natural logarithms, here the second one in the word

explanation.surface: Something about balls and second base, as if a baseball umpire were checking things.
explanation.walkthrough: Base is e, the base of natural logarithms; the second one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine or check it, and the third-person verb form matches examines.
